item.title: The Idempotent Measure Conjecture beyond solvable and stable groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pym's theorem [Pym62] states that a regular Borel probability measure on a locally compact group is idempotent if and only if it is the normalized Haar measure of a compact subgroup. The Idempotent Measure Conjecture, the definable-group counterpart of [GHK25, Conjecture (A)], proposes an analogous characterization: a global fim Keisler measure on a definable group is idempotent if and only if it is the unique global Keisler measure concentrating on a type-definable subgroup and invariant under translation by elements of that subgroup. We prove this conjecture for virtually solvable definable groups in arbitrary theories. More generally, we establish it for definable groups admitting a finite series of definable normal subgroups whose successive quotients are either virtually solvable or stably embedded with stable induced structure. Finally, we disprove [GHK25, Conjecture (A)] in its automorphism-group formulation in the theory of dense linear orders without endpoints.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Max Hoffmann

item.title: Weak $\lambda$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mr\'owka spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.11025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $\lambda$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $\lambda$-space is a $\lambda$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $\omega_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $\lambda$-set is a $\lambda$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>\omega_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Ismael Corral Rojas, Vinicius de Oliveira Rodrigues, Victor dos Santos Ronchim

item.title: Infinite sumsets via model theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove versions of (variations of) Erd\H{o}s sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.
item.dc:creator: Amador Martin-Pizarro, Daniel Palac\'in

item.title: Adding minimal fresh subsets to $\aleph_\omega$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_\omega$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $\omega$-sequence in $\aleph_\omega$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.
item.dc:creator: Moti Gitik, Mohammad Golshani

item.title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.12495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Aschenbrenner, Lou van den Dries, Joris van der Hoeven

item.title: Dynamic Topological Completeness for $\mathbb R^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic topological logic (${\bf DTL}$) combines topological and temporal modalities to express asymptotic properties of dynamic systems on topological spaces. A dynamic topological model is a triple $\left <X,f,V\right >$, where $X$ is a topological space, $f:X\to X$ a continuous function and $V$ a truth valuation assigning subsets of $X$ to propositional variables. Valid formulas are those that are true in every model, independently of $X$ or $f$. A natural problem that arises is to identify the logics obtained on familiar spaces, such as $\mathbb R^n$. Slavnov showed that any satisfiable formula could be satisfied in some $\mathbb R^n$ for $n$ large enough, but the question of how the logic varies with $n$ remained open. In this paper we prove that any fragment of ${\bf DTL}$ that is complete for locally finite Kripke frames is complete for $\mathbb R^2$. This includes ${\bf DTL}^\bigcirc$; it also includes some larger fragments, such as ${\bf DTL_1}$, where ``henceforth" may not appear in the scope of a topological operator. We show that satisfiability of any formula of our language in a locally finite Kripke frame implies satisfiability in $\mathbb R^2$ by constructing continuous, open maps from the plane into arbitrary locally finite Kripke frames, which give us a type of bisimulation. We also show that the results cannot be extended to arbitrary formulas of ${\bf DTL}$ by exhibiting a formula which is valid in $\mathbb R^2$ but not in arbitrary topological spaces.
item.dc:creator: David Fern\'andez-Duque

item.title: Projections between Ramsey quasi-orders and topological Ramsey spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Ramsey quasi-order is a quasi-order $(\cal{R},\leq)$ such that $\cal{R}$ is a Polish space, $\leq$ is analytic and every analytic subset of $\cal{R}$ is Ramsey. In this paper, we study the transfer of the analytic Ramsey property via monotone quasi-open maps, which are closely related to a family of forcing projections between quasi-orders (ranging from weak projections to strong projections). We apply this framework to the class of topological Ramsey spaces by providing a detailed list of examples of strong projections between topological Ramsey spaces, and show that, for many of these examples, there is no weak projection in the reverse direction. We also exhibit pairs of topological Ramsey spaces that do not weakly project into each other. Finally, partially confirming a conjecture of Dobrinen, we show that every space in a large class of topological Ramsey spaces either strongly projects into the Ellentuck space or contains a dense set of atoms.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Unger, Clement Yung

item.title: Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal
item.description: arXiv:2611.12848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $\kappa$ without adding bounded subsets to $\kappa$, while preserving $\kappa^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $\kappa$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.
item.dc:creator: Mirna D{\v z}amonja, Vladimir Kanovei

item.title: Topological Lifting of Mundici Equivalence and Di Nola--Lettieri Equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2611.10087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that summability characterises precisely when a topological MV-algebra can be realized as the unit interval of a lattice-ordered topological abelian group, thereby providing a topological lifting of both Mundici equivalence and DiNola--Lettieri equivalence. Applications include a Birkhoff--Kakutani-type metrisation theorem, a second-countability criterion, and a topological extension of a key continuity lemma from the proof theory of first-order {\L}ukasiewicz logic---following Baaz--Metcalfe's hypersequent approach to approximate completenesss---and provides an $A$-valued topological semantics for the approximate strong completeness of~$\mathbf{G}\text{{\L}}\forall$, where $A$ ranges over summable topological MV-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Jia, Yichuan Yang

item.title: A trace costs one quantifier: the exact complexity of perfect play in nonlocal games
item.description: arXiv:2611.10481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a finite nonlocal game, can the players win with certainty? We prove that the existence of a perfect normal spatial strategy is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete, even when restricted to games of value one, so it cannot be decided even with an oracle for the halting problem. This is strictly harder than perfect play in the finite-dimensional and commuting-operator models, which are $\Sigma^0_1$-complete and $\Pi^0_1$-complete. Within the commuting model, the existence of a perfect normal strategy with a finite or semifinite von Neumann host is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete, whereas for every fixed type $\mathrm{III}_\lambda$ subtype it has the same $\Pi^0_1$-complete language as unrestricted commuting play. A trace thus costs one existential number quantifier: the hardness constructions force every perfect strategy to choose a finite clock period or a finite tree depth. Spatial $\Sigma^0_2$-completeness also holds when finite entanglement entropy is required, and both forms are formally verified in Lean. For every computable $0<\alpha<1$, perfect spatial play with $\mathrm{Tr}\,h^\alpha<\infty$ for the reduced density $h$ is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete as well; these conditions form a strict ladder between finite rank and finite entropy. We also prove $\Sigma^0_2$-completeness for one-shot zero-error communication with normal entanglement, and construct a finite channel with zero-error codes of a given size each of which needs infinite entanglement entropy.
item.dc:creator: Seth Douglas, Nidhal Mghirbi

item.title: Revisiting the conjectures of Shapiro and Schanuel
item.description: arXiv:2611.11404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We tackle Shapiro's conjecture for exponential polynomials where the coefficients are polynomials, and show that it follows from Schanuel's conjecture. More concretely, given exponential polynomials $f$ and $g$ with infinitely many common zeros, we show that Schanuel's conjecture implies that there is an exponential polynomial $h$ vanishing precisely at all the common zeros of $f$ and $g$.
item.dc:creator: Paola D'Aquino, Sebastian Eterovi\'c

item.title: Discrete Distributions and Their Limit Theorems in the Surreal Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.11591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the discrete uniform, hypergeometric and binomial distributions to the surreal numbers, allowing infinitely many outcomes, chips and trials. A uniform distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ gives each outcome probability $1/\omega$; on the eventually periodic sets we define the needed sizes explicitly, obtaining a probability that is regular and strictly monotone. For an urn with infinitely many chips and finitely many draws, the hypergeometric distribution is within an infinitesimal of the binomial. With infinitely many trials, and under a hypothesis on factorials of omnific integers that we show can be satisfied, we prove a surreal de~Moivre--Laplace theorem, and we show that the hypergeometric distribution with infinitely many draws is locally normal with a finite-population correction. Near its center, it is relatively close to the binomial distribution if and only if the sampling fraction is infinitesimal, an exact form of a familiar rule of thumb. For rare successes we prove, without any hypothesis on factorials, a surreal Poisson limit theorem and describe urns with finitely many red chips, where the binomial approximation fails beyond the first success.
item.dc:creator: John Harris

item.title: When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals
item.description: arXiv:2611.11623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order. While well-ordered standing sets admit the naive, recursive definition of play, we found a surprising example showing that this approach fails for non-well-ordered ones, where local decision rules do not determine a unique global outcome. By requiring uniqueness of play, we aim to provide a natural framework for hat-guessing games on arbitrary standing sets. For the classical visibility model, it was previously known due to Glivick\'y that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed when $S$ is well-ordered. We prove the same result for backwards well-ordered sets, even in the case when $S$ has no first element. In the full-visibility version of the game, Glivick\'y proved that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed if the standing set has a first element. We extend this result to arbitrary nonempty standing sets.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel Heged\H{u}s, Benedek Kov\'acs

item.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings. As applications, we compute cohomology rings of several classifying spaces and loop spaces of spheres.
item.dc:creator: Arseniy Kryazhev

item.title: Properties of Public Announcements as Operators: Commutativity, Monotonicity, Idempotence, Fixed Points, and Stabilization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each formula $\varphi$, we introduce the public announcement operator $U_\varphi$, which maps every model to its updated model under the public announcement of $\varphi$. We then study its algebraic and dynamic properties with a particular focus on commutativity, monotonicity, idempotence, fixed points, and stabilization. Among many results, we show the following. First, monotonicity of $U_\varphi$ is characterized by a family of preservation conditions and equivalence to an existential formula. Second, there exists a formula that achieves every nonzero ordinal as a stabilization rank---the first stage at which a model stabilizes---of some model. Finally and unexpectedly, extinction of every model under iterated announcements of $\varphi$ is equivalent to common unknowability, being always informative when true, and a fixed point view of the Moore sentence. Over S5, those are further equivalent to common unbelievability and being always informative. Other results include characterizations of commutativity and strong commutativity, idempotence as success, properties of fixed points, and finite and $\omega$-stabilization. For analysis, we use PAL (state elimination) and BPAL (arrow elimination), clarifying their subtle differences.
item.dc:creator: Eiji Yamada

item.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.12365v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $\sigma$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.
item.dc:creator: C\"uneyt \c{C}evik

item.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.12469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Teheux

item.title: Absorbed Types and Derivations in Exponential o-Minimal Theories
item.description: arXiv:2511.13447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: I analyze $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate and $\mathcal{O}$-residual types in an o-minimal expansion of an ordered field $\mathbb{E}$, where $\mathcal{O}$ is a convex valuation ring. The main result is a characterization of those exponential theories $T$ such that for all $(\mathbb{E}, \mathcal{O})\models T_{\mathrm{convex}}$ the image of any $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate type is given by some composition of translations, sign changes and exponential, of some \emph{possibly different} $\mathcal{O}$-weakly immediate type. I call these theories \emph{transserial}, and they encompass simply exponential theories such as $T_{\exp}$ and $T_{an, \exp}$. A consequence of the analysis is that there are no counterexamples to \emph{Tressl's signature-alternative} (cf [15]) in models of transserial theories admitting an Archimedean prime model. The characterization has at its core some arguments that use very few but fundamental properties of the valued differential field of germs at a cut in an o-minimal structure. These are abstracted in some conditions of compatibility between the derivation and the order or the derivation and the valuation, both ultimately stemming from the mean-value-theorem in o-minimal structures. I develop some basic theory around these notions and observe that in the case of few constants (i.e.\ when the valuation ring contains the constants) these notions specialize to notions thoroughly studied in arXiv:1509.02588
item.dc:creator: Pietro Freni

item.title: Combinatorial Properties of the Raisonnier Filter
item.description: arXiv:2602.23340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Raisonnier filter is a combinatorial object isolated by Jean Raisonnier in order to simplify Shelah's proof that if all $\mathbf{\Sigma}^1_3$ sets are Lebesgue-measurable then there is an inner model with an inaccessible cardinal. In this paper, we study the combinatorics of a general version of the Raisonnier filter, with an eye to potential applications in descriptive set theory. We prove various results about the Raisonnier Filter generated by simple sets, and we study the ideals associated to the Raisonnier Filter being rapid and/or unbounded, connecting it to the null-additive and meagre-additive ideals studied by Pawlikowski and Shelah. Among the more interesting results is a converse to Raisonnier's theorem which indicates that Raisonnier's technique is unlikely to lead to similar results for other regularity properties. We also draw some conclusions regarding the Borel and dual Borel Conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Spyridon Dialiatsis, Yurii Khomskii

item.title: Relative stability, relative categoricity and internal covers
item.description: arXiv:2607.23314v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $T$ be a countable complete theory with a distinguished unary predicate $P$, and let $T^{P}$ be the theory of the $P$-parts of models of $T$ with the induced structure. $T$ is said to be relatively categorical or categorical over $P$ if any isomorphism between the $P$-parts of two models of $T$ lifts to an isomorphism of the models in question. We study the special case of relative categoricity where $T$ is internal to $T^{P}$ (that is, every model $M$ of $T$ is in the definable closure of $P(M)$ together with additional parameters from $M$). We first give a structure theory for such $T$: after passing to $T^{eq}$ and naming a parameter, $T$ is the same thing as a "pure torsor cover" of $T^{P}$, namely simply adjoining to $T^{P}$ a new sort for a torsor $S$ for a $\emptyset$-definable group $G$ in $T^{P}$, with no additional structure. We discuss relative stability, or stability over $P$, and give a characterization of relative stability, superstability, and $\omega$-stability of $T$ in terms of $H$ having the stable chain condition, superstable chain condition, and $\omega$-stable chain condition, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi, Anand Pillay

item.title: The consistency strength of the failure of amenable C-sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.09086v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the consistency strength of the existence of a regular uncountable cardinal carrying no amenable $C$-sequence. It is equiconsistent with the existence of an inaccessible cardinal $\kappa$ which is $\Pi^1_\xi$-indescribable for every $\xi<\kappa^+$ in the transfinite second-order hierarchy of indescribability. For the lower bound, we prove that the failure of amenability at $\kappa$ implies that $L$ contains such a cardinal at or below $\kappa$, using constructible guessing sequences, correct constructible levels, and a transfinite induction. For the upper bound, we prepare the cardinal so that every proper initial segment of a full Hechler iteration of length $\kappa^+$ preserves weak compactness. Each final $C$-sequence appears at a bounded stage and is captured at the next stage on a stationary set; the remaining closed iteration preserves that capture.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Fernandes

item.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
item.description: arXiv:2610.32038v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.
item.dc:creator: Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob

item.title: Model Existence and Scott's Theorem for Infinitary Real-Valued Logic: A Topological Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2611.02247v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we adopt a topological perspective to extend two theorems of classical infinitary logic to the infinitary logic of Keisler's general real-valued structures: the omitting types theorem and Scott's theorem. There the formulas need not be uniformly bounded, and no moduli of continuity are required, as they are in the metric extensions of the classical theorems; neither equality nor a metric is required. The omitting types theorem holds for every countable fragment, because the space of Henkin types of the fragment is \v{C}ech-complete. Scott's theorem characterizes every structure with countable sorts, among all structures, up to approximate equivalence, and the classes of this equivalence are Borel sets in the Polish space of structures on the natural numbers. With the monoid of surjections of the natural numbers in place of the group of permutations, we also prove L\'opez-Escobar's theorem for classical infinitary logic without equality.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Aubone, Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: A Side Condition Principle With Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.04362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a combinatorial principle $\textsf{SC}(\kappa)$, for any regular cardinal $\kappa \ge \omega_2$, which asserts the existence of a family $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq [H(\kappa)]^\omega$ of elementary substructures of $H(\kappa)$ which is closed under finite intersections and satisfies that for stationarily many $N \in \mathcal{Y}$, if $M \in \mathcal{Y}$ and $M \cap \omega_1 < N \cap \omega_1$, then $M \cap N \cap \kappa \in N$. We explore the idea of defining forcings with side conditions consisting of finite subsets of such a family $\mathcal{Y}$. If $\textsf{SC}(\omega_2)$ holds, then there exists a thin stationary subset of $[\omega_2]^\omega$, and consequently $\textsf{SC}(\omega_2)$ is independent of ZFC. Assuming that $\mu$ is a Mahlo cardinal, the L\'{e}vy collapse $\mathrm{Col}(\omega,<\mu)$ forces that $\textsf{SC}(\kappa)$ holds for all regular cardinals $\kappa \ge \omega_2$. Local instances of $\textsf{SC}$ can be forced using matrices of models or derived as consequences of square principles. We apply the principle $\textsf{SC}$ to define two kinds of forcings: a streamlined version of a strongly proper collapse, and a forcing which is strongly proper on a stationary set and adds arbitrarily many Baumgartner clubs. Finally, we prove two consistency results using forcings derived from $\textsf{SC}$ related to Aronszajn trees, the guessing model principle, strong failures of club guessing, and the higher dominating number.
item.dc:creator: Hannes Jakob, John Krueger

item.title: Infinitary real-valued logic and a refinement of the Kochen-Specker theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.05656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables in quantum mechanics is finite, including the obstructions that rest on Gleason's hypothesis of countable additivity. Since Kochen and Specker, such obstructions have been certified by finite configurations of rays, at the level of propositional logic: once a configuration is fixed, the obstruction is the inconsistency of finitely many Boolean constraints. Compactness, the source of these configurations, cannot reach the obstructions that rest on countable additivity: in infinite dimension the finite-dimensional events admit a finitely additive noncontextual valuation, and countable additivity constrains infinitely many events at once. The tool is a theorem of infinitary real-valued logic that takes the place of compactness: every countable theory of closed conditions without models is refuted by a well-founded tree of finite contradictions, given by the winning strategies of a model existence game. Quantum probability is axiomatized by such a theory, whose standard models are exactly those of Gleason's theorem. In the strategy we construct, a hypothetical noncontextual measure is not refuted by a configuration fixed in advance: through countable additivity, the measure itself selects the four-dimensional subspace in which the measure fails. The same logic defines, in the standard models, exactly the $\sigma$-projective sets of probabilities. Statements about $\sigma$-projective sets often go beyond ZFC, as the measurability of all these sets does; our theorems are nevertheless proved in ZFC, since the only determinacy they use is that of open games.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Aubone, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: The Logic of Emergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.06641v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: ``Emergence'' refers to the fact that different mathematical languages and theories seem to be required to describe scientific theories that operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Highly circumscribed, special cases of emergence have been investigated using many different formal tools, including coarse-graining (over space and / or time), renormalization, dimension reduction, broken symmetry, and various formulations of causality. Here we extend the mathematics of model theory to unify and extend these earlier investigations. As a preliminary application of our framework, we investigate canonical examples of emergence, including the emergence of genetics from chemistry, of psychology from neurobiology, and of different forms of collective behavior from the laws governing their constituent parts. By exploiting the power of model theory we also uncover many aspects of emergence that were previously obscured. In particular, we uncover some of the rich hierarchical structure that relates different scientific fields. For example, we show that scientific fields can be related via a collection of multiple partial orders, all defined over the same set. On the other hand, under an alternative relation among scientific fields, one which allows cycles, we show that it is possible that the set of all of scientific fields must collapse into a single scientific field. Going forward, these investigations point to the formal tools that might need to be developed in order to arrive at a deeper understanding of this emergent hierarchy of scientific reality.
item.dc:creator: David H. Wolpert, David C. Krakauer

item.title: A true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
item.description: arXiv:2611.07321v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehat{\phi}$ denotes its interpretation on $\omega$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehat{\phi}$ is a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Golshani

item.title: Path Types in Algebraic Type Theory
item.description: arXiv:2601.06567v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A new approach to the semantics of identity types in intensional Martin-L\"of type theory is proposed, assuming only a category with finite limits and an interval. The specification of \emph{extensional} identity types in the original presentation of natural models paralleled that of the other type formers $\Sigma$ and $\Pi$, but the treatment of the \emph{intensional} case there was less uniform. It was later reformulated to an account based on polynomials; here a further improvement in the style of the other type formers is achieved by employing an interval, in order to give a single pullback specification of a model with \emph{path types}. The interval is also used to specify a (Hurewicz) fibration structure on the universe of the model. It is shown that the combination of these two conditions suffices to model the intensional identity rules, assuming only finite limits. The addition of an interval also relates the current treatment to that of cubical type theory.
item.dc:creator: Steve Awodey, Joseph Hua

item.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for Horn Amalgamation
item.description: arXiv:2608.12206v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The amalgamation decision problem asks whether the finite models of a given universal first-order sentence have the amalgamation property. We prove that this problem is ExpTime-hard for universal Horn sentences of maximum relation arity three, and 2ExpTime-hard when the arity is unbounded, thereby strengthening the previous best lower bounds for universal Horn sentences. The first reduction simulates runs of nondeterministic tree automata using a single ternary relation and unary and binary auxiliary relations. The second simulates finite winning strategies in an exponential corridor game. As a secondary contribution, we prove that deciding the winner remains 2ExpTime-complete for the game normal form used in our reduction, in which each move label determines a unique legal successor from every non-winning legal row.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Rydval

item.title: $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-networks, $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizability, and local HCP-finiteness
item.description: arXiv:2609.30317v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every admissible ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, we prove that every regular space with a $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving (HCP) $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-metrizable, answering Problem~5.2 of Zhou--Liu--Liu--Lin. The proof combines existing characterizations with a local countability bound. If $y_n\to_{\mathcal{I}} x$ in a space $X$ and $\{n:y_n\ne x\}\in\mathcal{I}^{+}$, then every point-discrete family of $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is countable. If no such sequence exists at $x$, then $\{x\}$ itself is an $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhood. These alternatives imply that every space with a $\sigma$-point-discrete $\mathcal{I}$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal{I}$-$snf$-countable. We say that $\mathcal{I}$ has local HCP-finiteness if, in every $T_1$ space, the convergence and support assumptions above imply that each HCP family of $\mathcal{I}$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is finite. A countable Rudin--Keisler antichain of free ultrafilters gives an admissible ideal without this property, so the countability bound cannot in general be strengthened to finiteness. Every $P^{-}$ ideal has local HCP-finiteness. We give sufficient conditions for Fubini products, heterogeneous Fubini sums, and increasing unions to preserve this property. These results establish local HCP-finiteness for the finite Fubini powers of $\mathrm{Fin}$, Kat\v{e}tov's first limit-stage ideal $\mathrm{Fin}^\omega$ and its finite successors, the tree-derived rank-$\omega$ ideal $\mathcal H_{<\omega}$, and the inductive-limit ideal $\mathrm{Fin}_\omega$. All these examples except $\mathrm{Fin}$ fail $P^{-}$.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: A Non-Dichotomy for CSPs of Stable $\omega$-Categorical Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.19940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct countable, stable, $\omega$-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable $\omega$-categorical graphs $M_\alpha$ for suitable irrational parameters $\alpha>1$. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs $M_\alpha$ by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound $t$, there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME$(t)$. For an explicit parameter $\alpha$, the restriction to complete instances belongs to $\mathrm{coNP}$ and the full CSP belongs to $\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}$. Separating the ages of the $M_\alpha$ using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Bodirsky, David Bradley-Williams, Ehud Hrushovski, Christoph Spiess

item.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
item.dc:creator: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck
